statements.statement: A message queue ensures that messages are processed in the order they are received.
statements.explanation: Message queues typically process messages in a first-in, first-out (FIFO) order, meaning they are handled in the sequence they arrive.

statements.statement: Message queues are only useful when services are running on different machines.
statements.explanation: Message queues can be used for communication between components of a single application on the same machine, as well as services on different machines. They are not limited to distributed systems.

statements.statement: Using a message queue allows parts of a system to handle tasks asynchronously.
statements.explanation: Message queues enable asynchronous processing because the sender can continue executing without waiting for the receiver to handle the message. This decouples system components and allows them to work independently.

statements.statement: If a message queue is full, new messages are automatically discarded.
statements.explanation: Typically, if a message queue reaches its limit, new messages may be rejected or the queue may employ back-pressure mechanisms, but automated discarding is not a default behavior because it could lead to data loss.
